resources.string: No Bluetooth feature and no adapter: nothing to test.
FEATURE_BLUETOOTH is declared but there is no adapter: the Bluetooth service (com.android.bluetooth) did not start or crashed. Check logcat for BluetoothManagerService.
An adapter exists but FEATURE_BLUETOOTH is not declared: android.hardware.bluetooth.xml is missing from vendor/etc/permissions, so apps that need Bluetooth are hidden.
rfkill reports a hard block on Bluetooth: the power GPIO or the board switch keeps the chip off even though the stack thinks it is on.

Bluetooth did not reach ON within 8 s. This is usually the controller bring-up: firmware download (rampatch / nvm_tlv), UART/SMD transport, or the power sequence of the chip. Look for hci and bt_vendor timeouts in logcat.
Turn Bluetooth on from the area screen and run again. If it falls back to off by itself, the controller failed to start (firmware, transport, power).
A Bluetooth service is restarting in a loop. Read its tombstones and logcat: a crashing vendor HAL keeps the adapter from turning on.
The ROM hides the Bluetooth properties from apps. Not a fault.
Apps get 02:00:00:00:00:00 instead of the real address since Android 6, and the secure setting is restricted. Not a fault; read it from Settings → About phone or with adb.

The address is a known placeholder (all zeros, 00:00:00:00:5A:AD from Qualcomm NV defaults, or a test pattern): the real BD address is not provisioned. Every phone with this ROM will share it and pairing can mix devices up.
The adapter does LE but FEATURE_BLUETOOTH_LE is not declared: android.hardware.bluetooth_le.xml is missing, and apps for wearables, trackers and fitness bands will not install.
No multi-advertising and no offloading: typical of a Bluetooth 4.0 controller, or of a vendor HAL that does not report the LE capabilities (le_local_supported_features).
The list of paired devices could not be read.
Bluetooth is on but getBluetoothLeScanner() returned null: the stack does not support LE scanning on this controller.

The stack refused the LE scan. REGISTRATION_FAILED or INTERNAL_ERROR mean the controller rejected the scan commands (firmware or HAL); TOO_FREQUENTLY means more than 5 scans in 30 s: wait and run again.
Location is off: Android delivers no scan results to apps that may use them for location. Turn Location on and run again.

No BLE advertiser seen in 8 s. Almost every place has some (phones, TVs, earbuds, trackers): if there are some around, the controller is not receiving. Suspect firmware (rampatch/nvm), the antenna path, or a coexistence setting that keeps the radio on Wi-Fi.
Every device has the same RSSI (%1$d dBm): the controller or HAL reports a fixed value.
Some devices have impossible RSSI values (0 dBm or above, or below -120 dBm).
startDiscovery() returned false: the stack is not ready or the permissions are missing.
Discovery was accepted but never reported as started and found nothing: the controller does not run the HCI inquiry.
Inquiry ran but no classic device answered. Most phones and headsets are only discoverable while in pairing mode: put one in pairing mode and run again.
This device has no Bluetooth adapter.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on to scan; Android asks for confirmation.
Could not ask to turn Bluetooth on (%1$s).
BLE scan and classic inquiry together, 12 s
Grant the nearby devices and location permissions above to scan.
Location is off: scans may return nothing until you turn it on.
Put a headset or another phone in pairing mode to see classic devices too.
Classic discovery refused by the stack.
Grant the nearby devices permission to see the paired devices.
Pair a headset, earbuds or a speaker from the Bluetooth settings, then play some music and, if you can, make a short call.
Does it pair and play music cleanly, without dropouts or crackling?
During a call through the headset, do both sides hear each other?
